title: Canonical performance digest and pin validation playbook
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create a prescriptive playbook and automation for producing a canonical, signed performance digest for every model version accepted into the Redwood catalog. The digest will normalize latency/throughput/cost measurements across regions and hardware, include sampled workload traces and representative prompt sets, and provide deterministic checks that must pass before a model version can be pinned or published as a Redwood-verified profile. This ticket scopes the schema, validation rules, signing workflow, Git-backed storage path, canary validation steps, and developer/ops UX for failures and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Define JSON schema for canonical performance digest capturing: per-region latency P50/P95/P99, steady-state throughput at specified batch sizes, normalized cost-per-token, workload sample IDs, test harness config, and a checksum/signature field.
Automated CI job that validates incoming digests against schema and runs a fast sanity suite (smoke traces + cost sanity) within 2 hours of ingestion.
Digest is produced and signed for two recent onboarding cases (open-model v1.3 and v2.0) and pushed to the git-backed registry under canonical/2025/02/<model>-<version>.json.
Pin workflow requires passing digest validation, and a rollback knob exposing the previous pinned digest within Console rollouts UI.
Operational runbook documented: failure modes, SLA targets for validation, alert routing to oncall, and post-mortem checklist.
Telemetry contract defined so Console and runtime can read digest fields to display cost/latency anchors on model pages and enforce route-routing guards.
Performance digest signing key management documented and integrated with KMS/HSM used by Private deployments.
Stakeholders (Runtime leads, QA, Console, Security) have reviewed and signed off on playbook.

risks: Schema complexity could slow onboarding if the required samples are expensive to produce in CI.
Signed digests introduce key-management burden; key rotation or HSM outages could block publishes.
Normalization heuristics (cost adjustment between regions/hardware) may produce confusing anchors if not well documented.
Too-strict validation might cause false negatives for novel model architectures (e.g., very long context models).
Storage permission misconfiguration could leak unverified digests before signing.
decisions: Adopt a single JSON canonical digest schema rather than multiple format variants to simplify tooling.
Use Git-backed registry for immutability and audit trail; tag digests by date and model-version hash.
Signing will use existing enterprise KMS with HSM-backed keys for production; non-prod can sign with ephemeral test keys.
Fast sanity CI will run a constrained test set (<= 1k tokens total) to balance cost and signal; full validation runs will be scheduled offline.
Console will surface digest anchors (latency/cost) but visually mark region-normalized values and link to raw sample traces.
Pin gating will be controlled by a small set of boolean validators (schema, signature, smoke-pass, cost-sanity) to keep automation predictable.
